transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well... I suppose things have just gotten away from me. Since my wife’s fall, I mean. 

I’ve always been the man with the lists, the one with the plan. But lately... I just sit at the kitchen table. Staring at her medication chart. I don't really know why, but I find myself... snapping over nothing. Or getting emotional. And I'm just letting things go. The bills are piling up, I'm ignoring my mentoring calls, even the basic housework is just sitting there. I just... I can’t seem to make myself function.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting pleasure or interest from things that you usually enjoy, like hobbies, mentoring calls, or other activities?

I... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. 

I'm not sure it's about not enjoying things. Like I said, I just... haven't been doing them. I haven't really paid attention to how I feel about it.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the time, even when you're not thinking about your wife's situation?
I... I don't think so. I wouldn't really use the word sad. I just... I haven't noticed feeling like that, no. It's mostly just... what I said before.

Can you think back to when things were more normal—did you used to take pleasure in things like mentoring, your hobbies, or time with your wife, and do you still feel that same sense of enjoyment now?

I suppose I did enjoy those things, yes. Mentoring... it was important to me. But now... I don't know. Like I said, I'm just not doing them. I haven't really stopped to analyze if I'm enjoying them or not, because I'm just... not there. I'm just sitting at the table.
Have you noticed feeling down or blue, even when you're not thinking about your wife's accident or the situation with her health?
I... I thought I just answered that. No. I wouldn't say I feel blue. I'm just... dealing with what's happening. That's all.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions lately, even about simple things?
No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really had to make any big decisions lately anyway. I just sit there, so... there's not really much I need to concentrate on.
When you look back at the things you used to enjoy, like mentoring or your hobbies, do you still feel any sense of pleasure or satisfaction when you do them, even a little bit?
I... I thought we just went over this. I'm not doing them right now. So... no, I wouldn't really know if I feel satisfaction, because I'm just not doing them.
Even though you haven't been doing the things you used to like, like mentoring or your hobbies, do you still feel any interest in them, or have they lost their appeal entirely?
I don't... I don't know. I haven't really thought about it. They just... they aren't on my mind right now.
Even though you're not doing the things you used to enjoy right now, do you think you would feel any pleasure or satisfaction if you did them?
I really couldn't tell you. It's... hard to guess how I would feel about something I'm not doing. I just don't know.
Even if you’re not doing the things you used to enjoy right now, do you find that you still look forward to them, or does the idea of doing them not really mean much to you anymore?
I don't... look forward to much of anything right now. It just doesn't mean anything to me.
Even when you're not thinking about your wife's condition, do you find that things that used to bring you joy, like mentoring or your hobbies, just don't seem to matter to you anymore?
I suppose. I haven't really noticed. It's just... I don't care about any of it right now. I don't really know what else to tell you.
Even when you're not focused on your wife's situation, do you find that you can still experience pleasure or joy from things in general, or does everything feel kind of flat and meaningless?
I'm not sure. I don't really pay attention to whether I'm feeling joy or... whatever else. I just haven't noticed.

Can you think back to before your wife’s fall—did you used to take pleasure in things like mentoring, your hobbies, or other activities, and do you feel any of that same sense of enjoyment when you think about those things now?
I suppose I liked them fine back then. But now... I don't really sit around thinking about those things. So I couldn't tell you. I just don't.
Even when you're not focused on your wife's condition, do you find that you have completely lost interest in things you used to care about, like mentoring or your hobbies?
I don't know. I mean... I'm just not doing them. I haven't really thought about whether I care or not. It's just not on my mind.

Even when you're not thinking about your wife's situation, do you find that you have completely lost interest in things you used to care about, like mentoring or your hobbies, or do you think about them but just can't bring yourself to do them?

I... I don't really know how else to answer that. I'm not sitting around trying to force myself to do things and failing. I just... they don't cross my mind. So I don't do them. That's really all it is.
When you do, on rare occasions, find yourself doing something you used to enjoy—like mentoring or a hobby—do you still get any sense of pleasure or satisfaction from it, even a little bit?
I haven't actually done any of it. Like I said, I'm just not doing those things right now. So... I really couldn't tell you if I'd get anything out of it. I just haven't tried.

When you're not thinking about your wife's condition or the stress with her health, do you find that you're completely unable to feel pleasure or joy from anything at all, even small things like a good cup of coffee or watching the news?
I don't know... I mean, I still drink my coffee in the morning. It's fine, I guess. I'm just... not really paying attention to it. I'm just getting through the day.
Can you recall a time recently when you felt even a little bit better, even just for a short while, when things didn’t feel quite so heavy—even if just for a few minutes?
I don't... I don't really know. I'm not keeping track of moments like that. It's just... mostly the same, I guess. I haven't noticed.
Can you think of any moment in the past two weeks when you felt genuinely interested or engaged in something, even for a short time, not related to your wife’s condition?
No... nothing really comes to mind. The days just sort of blur together lately. I haven't been paying attention to much else.
